title: Voxel Blade Damage Calculator Architecture Tour
description: A guided walkthrough of the voxlblade-builder codebase, from application bootstrap to the core damage calculation engine.

steps.title: Application Bootstrap
steps.description: The app starts at src/main.ts, which mounts the Svelte 5 App component to the DOM and injects Vercel analytics. This is the single entry point for the entire application.

steps.title: Type Definitions & Data Contracts
steps.description: src/lib/types.ts defines all core TypeScript types — StatKey, StatMap, BuildState, Race, Guild, Armor, Ring, Rune, Enchantment, and Perk. These types are the shared contracts between the UI, state, and engine layers. The file also contains the applyUpgrade utility and STAT_KEYS/UPGRADE_MAX constants.

steps.title: Reactive State Management
steps.description: src/lib/store.ts creates a Svelte writable store for the entire BuildState (race, guild, equipment, enchantments, upgrades, etc.) with localStorage persistence. It exposes a derived 'result' store that runs calcBuild() whenever the build changes, plus helper functions like setEnchantment, moveArmorSlot, and moveRingSlot for safe state mutations.

steps.title: Game Data Definitions
steps.description: Data files define the game's entities: races/guilds/perks (character.ts), armors/rings/runes/enchantments (equipment.ts), and weapon blades/handles/gloves/essences (weapons.ts). These all import from JSON data files (races.json, blades.json, etc.) and export lookup functions like getRace, getBlade, getEnchant. Additional data modules define buffs (BuffData.ts), damage boosts (Boost.ts), DoT damage (DoTDamage.ts), perk/rune base damage (Perkbasedmg.ts, Runebasedmg.ts), summon stats (SummonData.ts), and weapon arts (weaponArts.ts).

steps.title: Engine Sub-modules
steps.description: The engine is split into focused modules: weapon.ts calculates base weapon damage from blades/handles/gloves/essences; enchant.ts applies enchantment stat modifiers and infusion bonuses; shrine.ts applies shrine multipliers to stats; format.ts provides stat formatting helpers; _utils.ts contains internal rounding utilities. The engine barrel (engine.ts) re-exports all of these.

steps.title: Core Damage Calculation Pipeline
steps.description: src/lib/engine/build.ts is the heart of the application. Its calcBuild() function orchestrates the entire damage pipeline: it resolves race/guild effects, assembles stats from equipped armor/rings/runes, applies enchantments and shrine multipliers, calculates weapon damage (normal + monk), computes critical hit chances via crit.ts, applies defense multipliers via defense.ts, processes all boost multipliers (level, emotional state, buffs, perks), calculates cooldown reductions, and resolves damage types. It pulls in BuffData, DoTDamage, Perkbasedmg, Runebasedmg, SummonData, and more to produce the final result.

steps.title: UI Component Layer
steps.description: The presentation layer is built with Svelte 5 components. App.svelte is the monolithic main component (~1100+ lines) containing all build selection UI, drag-and-drop armor/ring management, modal systems, and stat display. It imports directly from the engine barrel and store. Supporting components include DamageAnalyzer (damage breakdown analysis), BaseDamageCalc (base damage display), BuffList (active buff display), BuildSaves (save/load builds), and modals like WeaponPartModal for equipment selection.

steps.title: Data Flow Summary
steps.description: The full data flow: main.ts mounts App.svelte → App reads/writes the build store (store.ts) → store's derived 'result' calls calcBuild() in engine/build.ts → calcBuild aggregates data from engine/data/*, engine/weapon.ts, engine/enchant.ts, engine/shrine.ts, crit.ts, and defense.ts, plus game data from data/* modules → the computed result flows back reactively to App.svelte for display. The store auto-persists to localStorage.
